ground_truth_patient_facts: 2. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month.
3. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive.
4. He does not recall the episodes afterward.
5. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes.
6. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode.
7. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.
9. No prior seizures or neurological evaluations.
11. Lives with parents and one sibling.
12. No reported use of medications or exposure to toxins.
13. Denies fever, headache, visual or auditory disturbances, weakness, or other systemic symptoms.
ground_truth_exam_facts: 8. Motor: Normal tone, strength, and bulk in all four extremities.
9. Sensory: Intact to light touch, pinprick, vibration, and proprioception.
10. Coordination: No dysmetria on finger-nose-finger or heel-knee-shin tests.
13. Electroencephalogram: Interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the temporal lobes, more prominent on the right side.
14. MRI_Brain: No evidence of mass lesions, infarctions, or structural abnormalities.
